قَعَدَ مُسْتَفَزًّا [so in a copy of the S, but without the vowel-signs: in two other copies of the same, مُسْتَوْفِزًا, which belongs to art. وفز:] He sat in an uneasy posture. (S.) ―
-b2- فَرَسٌ مُسْتَفِزٌّ لِلْوَثْبِ وَالعَدْوِ [so in two copies of the S, in art. طمر; in the O, in that art., مُسْتَفِزُّ الوَثْبِ وَالعَدْوِ; probably a mistake for مُسْتَفَزّ; app. meaning, A horse in a state of excitement to leap and run.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
